content:
Hi,

Just trying to follow the rust-for-linux.com/contributing page and following up on some advice given from the Rust forums where I am trying to move some of my LKM's from C to Rust. These LKM's,basically create new address family protocols using (for starters) structs and functions like the following:

struct net_proto_family;
struct proto_ops;

// Add a socket protocol handler
err = sock_register(&proto_family);

These do not appear in the kernel crate. Per the submitting-new-abstractions-and-modules section in the contributions page, the second bullet point says to "check the mailing list archive" because "part of the work may be already done or in the process of being upstreamed", so I was hoping to see where things stand and get advice. I posted on the kernel lists but not expecting to get anything there.

I know the goals are not to duplicate or rewrite existing drivers, but my modules have not been opened up yet and still going through heavy development. I guess I am looking to know if there are proper API's or abstractions for the net subsystem, otherwise, I may want to start looking into contributing. It is also my understanding that we would not want to be directly using any C bindings, rather, using a Rust
abstractions layer.

Thank you for any advice.
